name: Mount Toubkal from Imlil
why: The highest mountain of North Africa, 4,167 m: up the Mizane valley past the shrine of Sidi Chamharouch to the stone refuge, then at dawn over scree to the summit tripod.
book: A licensed mountain guide is compulsory for foreigners. Night at the Toubkal refuge (CAF or Les Mouflons): book ahead. Taxi from Marrakech to Imlil (1.5 h).
water: Springs and drinks stalls up to the refuge; treat the water.
dangers: Altitude 4,167 m: headache or nausea, go down.
Snow and ice from November to April: crampons and ice axe.
Loose scree on the summit slope.
turnaround: Leave the refuge by 05:00 and turn back at 10:00 wherever you are.

points.name: Imlil
points.note: A Berber village of walnut trees, the gateway to Toubkal.

points.name: Sidi Chamharouch
points.note: A white-painted shrine on a boulder above the river, a pilgrimage site.

points.name: Toubkal refuge
points.note: Stone huts at 3,207 m at the foot of the summit slopes.

points.name: Toubkal summit
points.note: The 4,167 m top with its metal tripod.
